title: R' Yehuda ben Misparta
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In Sanhedrin 44a: Rabbi Ila'a said in the name of Rabbi Yehudah bar Mispartah that this teaches that Achan transgressed the five books of the Torah — Achan concealed his circumcision. In Yuchasin the reading before him was that R' Elazar said it in his name, and so it is in the Soncino printing. Hyman says it appears that it was written "R-A" and from this it became "R' Elazar." In Bereshit Rabbah, chapter 53, section 10, it is R' Yudan bar Mispartah. Hyman considers it plausible to say that he is R' Yehudah ben Sifra mentioned in Pesachim 70b, and reports that R' Ila'a said in his name that the festival offering overrides the Sabbath.
And in Chagigah, chapter 1, halakhah 6, he spoke in the name of R' Hoshaya, and from this Hyman infers that he was in the second generation of the amoraim of the Land of Israel.

And so he is mentioned in Yalkut on Psalms, end of the remez supplied as תתם (840 by ordinary letter values): "Rabbi Yehudah bar Mispartah said: whoever answers 'Amen' in this world, etc.", but in Tanchuma, Parashat Tzav, section 9, it reads R' Yehudah ben Gadia.

notes.text: The Yalkut locator is given as תתם and remains unresolved. Misparta, Sifra and Gadia are retained as source readings and Hyman’s proposed identifications.

All unsupported abbreviated personal titles, including the heading, Elazar twice, Yudan, Yehudah ben Sifra, Pesachim Ila'a, Hoshaya and Gadia, remain R'. The whole saved 186-character Davidson Sanhedrin 44a scalar explicitly names Rabbi Ila'a reporting Rabbi Yehudah bar Mispartah in the Achan circumcision statement, supporting those local names and titles only. It does not newly verify the five-books clause or Yuchasin/Soncino print history. Hyman's it-appears R-A-to-Elazar hypothesis, plausible Sifra identification and second-generation dating remain attributed arguments; no identity, chronology or print-history admission is made. Ben/bar and Mispartah/Sifra/Yudan/Gadia remain distinct. The supplied Yalkut label תתם remains beside ordinary letter-value 840 (400+400+40); the whole saved 300-character Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 840 scalar supports the Amen-in-this-world saying with full Rabbi Yehudah bar Mispartah locally. The supplied etc. is retained; no reward, scriptural proof, legal sequel or other continuation from either primary scalar is imported. The earlier 888 reading and unresolved-locator note remain historical, without retroactive PASS. The model's Psalm 106:48 assignment is rejected: its saved scalar quotes ברוך ה׳ לעולם אמן ואמן and does not establish that locator; no replacement Psalm number is supplied. Bereshit Rabbah 53:10, Pesachim 70b, Chagigah 1:6 and the Tanchuma Tzav 9 Gadia parallel were not newly checked. All historical English and notes, including the earlier mixed acronym claims, are preserved exactly; this additive qualification does not retire them. The p004 source hold remains.

The consulted scan of Hyman II, printed p. 564, has the affirmative דוחה שבת, “overrides the Sabbath,” as translated in his account. The whole consulted Davidson Pesachim 70b passage instead reads שאינה דוחה את השבת, “does not override the Sabbath,” under Yehudah ben Safra’s name in Ila’a’s report; the consulted Jerusalem Talmud Chagigah 1:6 passage likewise has a negative statement under Yehudah bar Safra in Hoshaya’s name. The English explicitly attributes the affirmative report to Hyman rather than silently harmonizing it. His proposed identification with Mispartah and his second-generation inference remain his arguments. Both the five-books and circumcision clauses in Sanhedrin 44a have now been read in full, as has the Yudan bar Masparta feast passage in Bereshit Rabbah 53:10. Hyman’s Yuchasin, Soncino and abbreviation-history claims have not been independently collated. The print confirms תתם, ordinary value 840, and the whole Yalkut 840 passage contains the Amen saying. The whole Buber Tanchuma Tzav 9 parallel names Yehudah bar Gadya, beside Hyman’s ben Gadia; these are compared readings, not an identity merger. No replacement Psalm locator or omitted reward, proof or legal sequel is inserted. The earlier notes remain verbatim and describe their preceding, more limited inspection.
